author: Sara Bell
description: The luxury industry is redefining status as consumers increasingly look beyond logos to craftsmanship, provenance and the origins of what they buy. RIISE’s Sara Bell argues that luxury’s future will depend on whether brands can connect rising prices to tangible proof of value, from exceptional materials and human skill to transparent supply chains and lasting design.
title: At Paris Fashion Week, Luxury Has to Prove What It’s Worth

author: Carlo Pignataro
description: For decades, luxury houses have expanded from products into stores, hotels, restaurants and other experiences. From Dior’s Milan flagship to Dubai’s transformation into a luxury capital, international luxury expert Carlo Pignataro explores how the most enduring brands can become something clients don’t simply see or buy, but experience and return to.
title: Eat Dior, or Eat at Dior? How Luxury Brands Are Building Beyond the Product

author: Mary Gregory
description: Making climate-conscious art at scale and in public is arduous, expensive and often exhausting. Agnes Denes, Mary Mattingly, Maya Lin and their peers have built substantial careers, sustain themselves through their practices and hold places in major collections, yet haven't shied away from creating works that help the planet.
title: Five Artists Who Treat the Earth as Both Medium and Beneficiary

author: Elisa Carollo
description: The trail expands on the $1.4 billion tri-government investment reshaping Toronto's waterfront through flood protection, environmental restoration and new public spaces. LAT's curator, November Paynter, told Observer that the curatorial process began while the park was still under construction, with the team researching the site's engineering, natural environment and history, before conducting studio visits with artists whose practices could respond to those conditions.
title: Toronto’s Lassonde Art Trail Reimagines Public Art as Part of a Healthier Urban Ecosystem

author: Elisa Carollo
description: The auction house’s newly appointed chief executive plans to leverage Freeman's strong local networks and estate expertise, along with new technology and a less rigid auction calendar, to compete with larger rivals without chasing every trophy consignment.
title: Freeman’s New CEO Muys Snijders Is Betting on Regional Roots and a Wider Reach

author: Elisa Carollo
description: 'Châtaignier en fleurs roses et blanches' leads a dozen Impressionist and Post-Impressionist masterpieces by Cézanne, Renoir, Degas and their peers owned by the Argentine sugar dynasty—a consignment long coveted by the major houses.
title: Sotheby’s Lands the $450 Million Blaquier Collection, Led by a $180M Van Gogh

author: Allie Lebos
description: From swanky speakeasies to Michelin-starred restaurants, we’re covering the very best of dining, drinking and doing in Hollywood.
title: Lights, Camera, Action: An Insider’s Guide to L.A.’s Historic Hollywood Neighborhood

author: Saleah Blancaflor
description: Josh Kushner's Thrive Capital valued A24 at $3.5 billion in 2024. Two years later, a $400 million hit in 'Backrooms,' a $75 million Google A.I. investment and a two-year Dior partnership suggest his bet on a studio as a brand is paying off.
title: Josh Kushner Valued A24 at $3.5 Billion. Dior and Google Just Proved Him Right.

author: Tim Keary
description: Safra Catz stepped down as Oracle's CEO "when things are great." A year later, the cloud business she championed is booming, but investors are questioning the cost of its A.I. buildout.
title: Safra Catz Made Oracle an A.I. Giant, Then Stepped Aside. One Year Later, How Has Oracle Fared?
